# UK Independence Party Manifesto 2005: Summary

## Core Mission: Restoring British Sovereignty

The UK Independence Party positions itself as the only political force willing to acknowledge that Britain is effectively governed from Brussels. Their fundamental purpose is withdrawing from the European Union to restore parliamentary sovereignty to Westminster—a position they frame as entirely reasonable and democratic.

UKIP emphasises they are not anti-European but believe the British people should govern themselves. Their 2004 European election success, with 2.6 million votes, demonstrated significant public support for an independent Britain free from EU control.

## The Case Against EU Membership

The manifesto argues the EU is not merely a trading arrangement but a political project systematically absorbing national government functions. EU "harmonised" rules allegedly account for 70% of British laws, covering farming, fishing, taxation, and increasingly justice, defence, and foreign policy.

UKIP characterises the EU as undemocratic, corrupt, and unreformable—a one-way street toward European government that strangles individuals and businesses with ill-conceived regulation. All establishment parties, they contend, maintain the fiction that the EU can be reformed in Britain's interests.

## Broader Ideological Stance

Beyond EU withdrawal, UKIP opposes the culture of bureaucratic control, performance targets, uncontrolled immigration, over-regulation, and political correctness that suppresses dissent. They champion smaller government, local accountability, individual responsibility, and traditional British values of trust, pride, and mutual respect—values they believe require no "modernisation."

## Economic Vision

UKIP promises continued EU trade through bilateral agreements while strengthening Commonwealth and global trading relationships. They advocate wholesale deregulation, particularly benefiting small businesses strangled by approximately 100,000 EU-originated regulations since 1973.

The party proposes using Britain's £12 billion annual EU contribution to raise state pensions, alongside tax cuts including halving council tax, scrapping the 10% income tax bracket, and raising inheritance tax thresholds. They favour eventual flat-tax implementation and simplified taxation.

## Public Services and Welfare

On healthcare, UKIP demands removing central government from NHS day-to-day management, restoring matron authority, and freeing doctors from bureaucratic targets. They advocate reforming the welfare system to reduce means-testing and restore dignity through independence from benefits.

For education, they propose greater school autonomy, scrapping centralised testing regimes, restoring discipline, and expanding private school access through assisted places and vouchers.

## Immigration and Law Enforcement

UKIP advocates approaching "zero net immigration" through strict controls, points-based work permits, "Britishness" tests, reinstated border controls, and rigorous deportation enforcement. They reject the suggestion that immigrants are needed to support an ageing population.

On law and order, they promise visible policing, credible sentencing, locally accountable police forces, and resistance to EU judicial harmonisation including Corpus Juris provisions.

## Agriculture, Defence, and Sovereignty

The party promises replacing CAP subsidies with guaranteed minimum prices, restoring British fishing waters, and rebuilding agricultural independence. On defence, they advocate increased military spending, NATO commitment, and complete withdrawal from EU common defence arrangements.

UKIP rejects regional government, supports referendums on major issues, and proposes repealing the Human Rights Act in favour of British common law traditions—ultimately envisioning a deregulated, self-governing Britain with restored traditional values and family stability.
